source.report_title: From alert to agency: What turns warnings into action?

methodology.weight: PROJWT population-projection weight; weighted numerator divided by the full applicable subgroup denominator.
methodology.warning_base: WP24181 is non-null; all eight channel variables are required on this base. A code 1 on any channel means warned; codes 2, 97, 98 and 99 remain in the denominator and count as no warning.
methodology.action_base: Respondents with at least one warning; WP24215 codes 1, 2, 98 and 99 remain in the denominator. Ability to act is code 1.
methodology.channel_count: Count of the eight channel items answered yes (code 1), among warned respondents; compare exactly one, two and three channels.
methodology.plan_and_agency: Among warned respondents with binary yes/no answers to both WP23345 and WP22252. WP22252 code 3 (it depends), DK and refused are excluded from this grouping; WP24215 DK/refused remain in each action denominator.
methodology.income_groups: CountryIncomeLevel codes 1-4 only; code 9 (not classified) is excluded. WP24215 DK/refused remain in each action denominator.
methodology.missingness: The publisher reproduction uses WP24181 non-null as the asked base; all eight channel values must be present together on that base and absent outside it.

interpretation.statement: Multiple warning channels and household preparedness/personal agency are associated with higher self-reported ability to act. This cross-sectional retrospective survey does not identify causal effects.

limitations: This is an independent arithmetic reproduction of selected published aggregates from the publisher's public 2025 microdata, not an independent survey.
The survey is retrospective and self-reported; it does not verify warning timestamps, delivery, comprehension, actual protective action or avoided loss.
The channel-count and plan/agency gradients are descriptive associations, not causal effects; hazard severity, resources, exposure and other confounders may differ between groups.
No design-based confidence intervals are calculated in this reproduction; one-decimal point estimates must not be read as precise individual or country predictions.
The publisher's 2025 wave includes 143,459 respondents across 140 countries and territories; China used an opt-in web panel and should be interpreted under the publisher's methodology note.
Georgia's warning-question base is 99, below the publisher's n>=100 country-ranking threshold; no Georgia national effectiveness estimate is inferred.
The dataset is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0; only small aggregate results and attribution are stored here, not respondent-level records.
